=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/implement_heal_preflight.sh:support_fallback block (approx. line 100) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The right operand of `[ ... != ... ]` is an unquoted glob pattern. Under bash's test builtin, pathname expansion applies, so the literal token `main` is interpreted as a pattern. If the script's CWD contains any file matching `main*` (for example `maintenance/`, `main.bak`, or a tracked `main` branch alias), the pattern expands and the comparison can incorrectly evaluate to `not equal` when `expected_ref=main`, incorrectly setting `support_fallback=true` and producing a spurious fallback warning / `detail=support_ref_fallback` refusal.
  WHY: This is the documented command shape used in `scripts/implement_heal_preflight.sh` directly (not inside a `case` arm), and the script runs from the workflow workspace that may contain directories whose names happen to start with `main`. With an expansion hazard present, the `support_fallback` heuristic silently produces wrong values on those runs, which propagates into the `HEAL_SCOPE_REFUSED` log line and the `::warning::Heal support source came from the main fallback checkout` notice.
- scripts/implement_heal_preflight.sh:refuse_support_ref function (approx. lines 124-132) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: When `support_fallback=true`, the function unconditionally overwrites the caller-supplied `detail` (`support_ref_unresolved` or `support_ref_mismatch`) with the single token `support_ref_fallback`. The specific cause that the case statement detected — e.g. that `refs/heads/stable` did not exist, or that the SHA comparison failed — is dropped from both the stderr error line and the issue comment marker. The context field still carries `fallback=true`, so an operator reading the log can infer that the fallback path was active, but the loss of the underlying diagnostic means a downstream alert or grep on `support_ref_unresolved`/`support_ref_mismatch` will not see those occurrences when fallback is in effect.
  WHY: This is a code-level behavioural decision, not a transitive inference — the function literal assignment happens at line `detail=support_ref_fallback` and the value is what reaches `refuse()`. Two distinct runtime paths (the branch ref cannot be resolved, vs. the SHA comparison fails) collapse to one detail token whenever the support checkout has a `main` branch present, hiding the actual fault.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: NONE — the PR implements every concrete deliverable in the linked issue specification: the `detail=` token is added on every refuse path; support-ref fallback is detected and reported through `support_fallback=true` plus the `::warning::` notice; expected/actual ref and SHA are logged through `set_support_context` using only charset-validated values; success and fail-closed behaviour is covered by `tests/test_implement_heal_preflight.py`; existing checks and required validation are preserved (the original `refuse malformed`, `refuse unavailable`, `refuse <status>` calls and their outcomes are intact); edits are confined to the two paths the spec authorises (`scripts/implement_heal_preflight.sh`, `tests/test_implement_heal_preflight.py`).
  Expected change site: Not applicable.
  Evidence of absence: The TASK_GAP raised by another reviewer regarding the new issue's `files_touched:` grant concerns the prior issue-creation step (the re-issue that produced this PR), not the implementation diff itself. By construction this PR is gated on `implement.yml` parsing an exact `files_touched:` grant that names both edited paths; the implement workflow would have refused the run before commit otherwise, and the slop-scan / check-runs snapshot shows the diff has proceeded to review on the head SHA, which means the gate accepted it. Re-asserting the grant inside this PR would duplicate a check that is structurally bound to a different workflow step.
